newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures erases gains to end mainly weaker.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures erases gains to end mainly weaker.

text.p: NYCE frozen concentrated orange juice futures ended lower for the third consecutive session Thursday, as a late bout of local selling dragged the January and March positions to fresh life-of-contract lows, traders said.
The market spent the bulk of the session above unchanged, but traders said January ran into strong resistance at the session high of 98.25 cents a lb.
"We can't get any upward momentum in the market," one trader said. "The market continues to look weak."

The most-active January contract closed down 0.05 cent a lb at 96.55, having ranged from 98.25 to 96.30, a new contract low. Second-month March also hit a new life of contract low of 99.25, before ending 0.10 weaker at 99.50. The back months finished 0.30 lower to 0.05 higher.
Traders said much of the day's selling was options-related, with high open interest in January 100.00-cent puts keeping a lid on the market.
As of Wednesday, open interest in the January 100.00 puts was 4,389 lots. January options expire December 6.

On the fundamental front, a U.S. agricultural attache pegged Brazil frozen concentrated orange juice output for marketing year 1996/97 at 1.055 million tonnes, down from 1.085 million tonnes seen for the previous season due to the lower amount of fruit delivered for processing.

The attache also estimated Brazil 1996/97 orange crop at 401 million 40.8 kilogram boxes, down 0.5 percent from a previous forecast and versus 405 million boxes estimated for the prior marketing year.
Volume was thin at an estimated at 1,200 lots compared with Wednesday's official volume of 2,636 lots.
